solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Man cornered in fortress?

definitions.meaning: a chess man that begins the game in a corner square of the board, the rook
a fortified stronghold, the home of a medieval lord

explanation.surface: Someone trapped inside a stronghold with no way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a chess piece, not a person: the rook starts in a corner and is also called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortress and a chess rook both go by this word, the second being the piece that starts in a corner.

clue.text: Monument not cheap to repair

indicators.note: something needing repair is broken, so these letters are to be put together again in a new order

explanation.surface: A war memorial will cost a lot to restore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to repair' rearranges the eight letters of NOT CHEAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph is a memorial monument to those buried elsewhere, typically the war dead.

clue.text: Expert on drinking has battle with organ, though not heart

parts.note: the Somme was a First World War battle in northern France

indicators.note: the heart of the organ word, its central letter, is to be left out

parts.note: the liver is a bodily organ

explanation.surface: A drinks expert has fought a battle with his liver, if not his heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though not heart' removes V, the middle letter of LIVER, leaving LIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sommelier is the wine waiter, a specialist in wines and drinking them with food.

clue.text: Note in top song

indicators.note: the note letter is placed inside the word for top

parts.note: a lid is the top of a jar or box
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A note found in the best song of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' looks like 'best', but it is a lid.
explanation.definitionFit: A lied is a German art song, as by Schubert, usually for voice and piano.

clue.text: Wood lays head on bosom

indicators.note: in an across answer the head is placed on, after, the bosom word

parts.note: the bosom is the chest
nut is slang for head

explanation.surface: Someone rests their head on another's breast.
explanation.definitionFit: Chestnut is a timber, the wood of the chestnut tree.

clue.text: Both outsiders reside abroad in location off mainland Scotland

indicators.note: abroad means all over the place, so these letters are scattered into a new order
the outsiders of a word are its first and last letters, here of the word Both

explanation.surface: Both of two outsiders live overseas, off the Scottish coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outsiders' takes B and H from Both; 'abroad' mixes them with RESIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrides are island groups lying off the west coast of the Scottish mainland.

clue.text: Eye perhaps no good with ears and nose after surgery

indicators.note: surgery reshapes things, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: N is short for no, as on a Y/N form

explanation.surface: A doctor says an eye operation went badly, with ears and nose also affected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eye' is one example of the class, hence 'perhaps'. N for no lands at the end, so only G with the ear and nose words is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The eye is an example of a bodily organ of sense, like the ear or nose.

clue.text: Unable to catch some players in group

definitions.meaning: having ..., so unable to catch fish or butterflies

explanation.surface: A fielder cannot hold the ball when some of the team bunch together.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer is NO NET: with no net you cannot catch anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is an ensemble of nine performers, and split in two it says you lack a net.

clue.text: In brief, Egyptian king less prepared for fight

indicators.note: a brief word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Tut is the short name of the pharaoh Tutankhamun

indicators.note: the letters of less are dressed or prepared afresh, into a new order

explanation.surface: A pharaoh, briefly described, was poorly ready for battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In brief' cuts TUT to TU; 'prepared' rearranges LESS as SSLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussle is a scuffle or vigorous struggle, a synonym for fight.

clue.text: Examine head in autopsy, cheerily

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: A cheerful pathologist examines the head during a post-mortem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters spanning autoPSY CHeerily.
explanation.definitionFit: To psych someone is to psychoanalyse them, informally examining what is in their head.

clue.text: More than one song book

definitions.meaning: songs in a show or set are called musical pieces of this kind
the fourth book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A collection of songs printed in a single volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Songs in a set are numbers, and Numbers is a book of the Bible.

clue.text: Split items not all there

definitions.meaning: the fruit in a banana split dessert

explanation.surface: Some divided goods are missing pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana split dessert uses this fruit, and 'gone bananas' means mad, not all there.

clue.text: River bait, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: signals a word heard rather than written, matching the river's name

parts.note: to bait someone is to tease or taunt them

explanation.surface: An angler asks whether a river is good for bait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bait' looks like fishing, but it is the verb to taunt. The Tees is a river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tees is a river in north-east England flowing into the North Sea at Middlesbrough.

clue.text: For example, sharp header from Aberdeen, and Celtic beaten

indicators.note: the header of a word is its opening letter, here of Aberdeen
beaten means knocked about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A football report: a sharp header from an Aberdeen player, and Celtic lose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'header from' takes A from Aberdeen; 'beaten' rearranges AND CELTIC. Aberdeen and Celtic are Scottish football clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a sharp, flat or natural sign added before a note outside the key signature is an accidental.

clue.text: Cross after selection, very old opener?

indicators.note: the crossing word comes after the selection word

parts.note: a draw is a selection made by lot
to bridge a gap is to cross it

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed after being picked for a team, with an ancient first batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' is not a batsman or a first move: it is something that opens, here the entrance to a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawbridge is the medieval hinged bridge lowered to open a castle's gateway.

clue.text: Those are gripping ballet moves, dancer finally admitted

indicators.note: the letter is let into the middle of the ballet moves

parts.note: a plié is a ballet move bending the knees

indicators.note: takes the closing letter of the word dancer

explanation.surface: Ballet moves are thrilling, with a final dancer let into the troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' looks like 'thrilling', but the definition means these things grip.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliers are a hand tool for holding things, so they are gripping by design.

clue.text: Country girl in a state?

definitions.meaning: a state in the south-east USA

explanation.surface: A rural girl gets herself worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' looks like 'upset', but it means one of the US states.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgia names a Caucasus nation, a US state and a girl.

clue.text: Irritated, Mudd is over case

indicators.note: in a down answer the first part sits over the second

parts.note: the setter Mudd speaking of himself says I am, I'M
a patient is a medical case

explanation.surface: The setter confesses he is annoyed about a matter.
explanation.walkthrough: Mudd is this puzzle's setter, so 'Mudd is' gives I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Being irritated and short of patience is being impatient, a near synonym.

clue.text: On study programme, seeking advice

parts.note: re means on, concerning
a course is a programme of study

explanation.surface: A student on a course looking for guidance.
explanation.definitionFit: Having recourse to someone is turning to them for help or advice.

clue.text: In portrait with bandaging, not Van Gogh's right approach

parts.note: something in a portrait has been drawn

parts.words: with bandaging, not Van Gogh's right
parts.note: Van Gogh cut off part of his left ear, which he painted bandaged; the one not his right is the left ear

explanation.surface: A portrait shows Van Gogh with a bandage, but not on his right side.
explanation.walkthrough: Van Gogh painted himself with a bandaged ear after cutting part of his left one off.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw near is to come closer, the same as to approach.

clue.text: Sycophant, one acting like a baby?

definitions.meaning: a fawning flatterer who creeps up to superiors
a baby moves on hands and knees before it can walk

explanation.surface: A flatterer is being childish.
explanation.definitionFit: A creep who grovels and a baby on all fours both answer to this word.

clue.text: One has very little uranium in organ

indicators.note: the uranium letter goes inside the organ word

parts.note: a newspaper is an organ, a medium of news or opinion
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A body part has only a trace of uranium inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' is a publication, not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A pauper is a very poor person, someone with almost nothing.

clue.text: Book showing hydrogen in organic compound

indicators.note: the hydrogen letter goes inside the compound word

parts.note: an ester is an organic compound made from an acid and an alcohol
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A chemistry text shows hydrogen in an organic compound.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is a book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: End up north of Michigan in US city

indicators.note: in a down answer the first part sits above the second
in a down answer the word for end is read upwards

parts.note: an aim is an end, a goal
MI is the postal abbreviation for Michigan

explanation.surface: Finish up north of Michigan, in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AIM into MIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami is a large city in Florida, in the United States.

clue.text: Second cup in store, broken

indicators.note: a broken thing is smashed apart, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A second cup in the shop has been smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like 'another', but it is the second note of a scale.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the supertonic is the second degree of a diatonic scale.

clue.text: Seed with two wings that forms within a shell

parts.note: a pea is a seed
R and L, right and left, the two wings or sides

explanation.surface: A winged seed develops inside a husk.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl grows inside an oyster shell, building up around an irritant.

clue.text: Tipping to the left, adds water to dish

indicators.note: in an across answer the word is turned to read leftwards

parts.note: to wet something is to add water to it

explanation.surface: A cook tilts a pan and adds water to the dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tipping to the left' turns WETS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stew is a dish of meat and vegetables slowly cooked in liquid.

clue.text: A little shoemaker turning up in little jumper

indicators.note: in a down answer the letters are read upwards

parts.note: in the fairy tale The Elves and the Shoemaker, little elves make the shoes

explanation.surface: A small cobbler appears wearing a little sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a sweater, as Britons call one, but it is a hopping insect. 'turning up' reverses A ELF.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a tiny insect that leaps great distances.

clue.text: Frost appearing with communist revolutionary, one giving nothing away

parts.note: hoar is frost

indicators.note: revolving the word turns it backwards

parts.note: a red is a communist

explanation.surface: A cold communist rebel who will not share anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns RED into DER.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarder stockpiles things and keeps them, never parting with any.

clue.text: Story inspired by greater dramatist

indicators.note: inspired is breathed in, so the story goes into the word for greater

parts.note: more means greater
a story is a lie, a fib

explanation.surface: A tale was drawn from a greater playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspired' means breathed in, so the fib is taken inside the word for greater.
explanation.definitionFit: Molière was the great seventeenth-century French playwright of comedies.

clue.text: Freed, evil snakes in grass

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed inside the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

indicators.note: to snake is to wind about, so these letters twist into a new order

explanation.surface: Evil snakes have been let loose in the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snakes' looks like reptiles but is a verb, meaning wriggles into a new order; 'in' then places the result inside the grass word.
explanation.definitionFit: Relieved of a burden or duty means freed from it.

clue.text: Beam brighter in the end then

indicators.note: takes the closing letter of the word brighter

parts.note: after means then, later

explanation.surface: A light beam that grows brighter at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beam' looks like a ray of light, but it is a roof timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A rafter is a sloping roof beam.
